target_customer: Initially bitcoin traders, later institutions, hedge funds, banks and fintechs
problem: Bitcoin prices differed by exchange and traders lacked transparency. SFOX routes trades across exchanges with algorithms, later becoming an institutional prime broker.
business_model: Trading fees and prime brokerage services
product_category: Crypto trading platform and prime broker

founders.name: Akbar Thobhani
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2014-08-23) says he left Airbnb to start the company.

founders.name: George Melika
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch and on the YC page.

competitors.name: CampBX
competitors.what: Atlanta bitcoin exchange operating as a single closed exchange

competitors.name: btcReport
competitors.what: iOS app comparing bitcoin prices across exchanges without trading

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi exchange order routing, limit orders and funds handling in an early, unregulated market.

defensibility.rationale: Routing algorithms were copyable, but liquidity connections, custody and later licenses built a moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch 2014 named Coinbase and Bitstamp as price venues. SFOX survived and pivoted to institutions.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2014: founder saw buying bitcoin cost more than a credit card purchase due to opaque pricing across exchanges.

branding.name_origin: Stands for San Francisco Open Exchange; Berkeley case study says founders wanted to build an open platform for financial products.

identity.visual_style: Now styled sFOX with a lowercase s
identity.voice_and_tone: Institutional, security focused (claims zero security incidents since 2014)

brand_strength.rationale: Acronym brand known in institutional crypto circles via press releases; no sourced consumer awareness.

pivots.from: retail bitcoin price comparison and routing
pivots.to: institutional crypto prime broker and infrastructure
pivots.why: Company now targets fintechs, banks, exchanges and asset managers per its site; timing not dated by a source

outcome_analysis: SFOX began as a retail bitcoin routing tool in 2014, raised a 22.7 million dollar Series A in 2018 and repositioned as an institutional prime broker with custody through a Wyoming trust. It survived crypto winters without reported shutdown, appointed a new CEO per its news page, and obtained a Singapore in principle approval in 2025. Pivot and compliance moat drove survival.
notes: Series A stated by Bitcoin Magazine and Cointelegraph; investor list from search summaries of these. Later rounds not searched so coverage is partial. Outcome search found no shutdown, acquisition or layoffs. Melika surname spelling varies across sources. Pivot date unknown.
